payload.source_label: Every vector in R^m decomposes uniquely as a linear combination of the eigenvectors

contract.statement: For a constant real m × m matrix satisfying the stated hyperbolicity condition, fix its corresponding m linearly independent eigenvectors. Every vector in R^m has exactly one real coefficient expansion in this fixed family. This is the selected sentence on raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, immediately following the hyperbolicity definition; the matrix and state-space setting comes from equation (1.1) and its following paragraph on raw PDF page 23, printed page 1. The assertion does not choose a canonical eigenbasis.
assumptions: A has real eigenvalues and a corresponding set of m linearly independent eigenvectors, as required by the immediately preceding definition of hyperbolicity (raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, hyperbolicity-definition sentence).
The linear combinations are in the real state space inherited from (1.1) (raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, q: R × R → R^m; raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, 'any vector in R^m').

The PDE setting explains the role of A and R^m; the selected conclusion is a linear-algebra statement about every state vector and does not require a chosen solution q (raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, (1.1); raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, 'any vector in R^m').

The subsequent explanation connects the decomposition to waves and eigenvalues to propagation speeds, with details deferred to Chapter 3; these are adjacent context (raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, sentences beginning 'As we will see' and 'The corresponding eigenvalues').
quantifiers: m is the number of components and the dimension of the real state space (raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, paragraph following (1.1)).
A is a constant real m × m matrix (raw PDF p.23, printed p.1, paragraph following (1.1)).

Fix the corresponding set of m linearly independent eigenvectors of A mentioned in the hyperbolicity definition; writing them as r_1,...,r_m is analyst-introduced indexing (raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, anchors 'corresponding set' and 'these eigenvectors').

For every v in R^m, quantify the coefficients of its expansion in that fixed family; writing the coefficient vector as a in R^m is an explicit mathematical rendering of the prose (raw PDF p.25, printed p.3, anchor 'any vector in R^m').
